summary: This is a VS Code development container configuration file that sets up a Python development environment running in Docker. It specifies which Docker container to use, installs a curated list of VS Code extensions for Python development, and configures editor settings like code formatting, linting, indentation, and language-specific behaviors to enforce consistent code style across the project.

explanations.3: This references a Docker Compose file located one directory level up that defines the actual Docker services and containers.
explanations.6: This specifies which service from the Docker Compose file should be used — in this case, the one named 'app_python'.
explanations.7: This sets which user account inside the Docker container will own and run the development environment, rather than using root.
explanations.8: This sets the default folder that opens when you connect to the container, essentially your project's home directory inside Docker.
explanations.11: This list installs specific VS Code extensions automatically when the development container starts, so you don't have to install them manually.
explanations.43: The 'settings' object contains configuration rules for how the editor should behave, organized by file type in square brackets like '[python]' or '[dockerfile]'.
explanations.45: This ensures that Dockerfile line endings use Unix-style newlines (\n) instead of Windows-style, preventing version control confusion.
explanations.67: This tells VS Code to automatically fix all fixable linting issues whenever you save a Python file.
explanations.68: This automatically reorganizes your Python import statements into a standard order when you save, keeping imports tidy.
explanations.85: This configures the spell checker to validate against English, French, and Dutch dictionaries.
explanations.88: This is a fallback rule for all file types to run code fixes only when explicitly requested, not automatically on save.
explanations.102: These numbers set vertical guide lines at columns 120 and 70 to help you see when lines are getting too long.
explanations.106: This enables sticky scroll, which keeps your current function or class definition visible at the top of the editor as you scroll down.
explanations.118: This hides certain folders from the file explorer sidebar (like .cache and .git) to reduce clutter.
explanations.129: This passes a configuration file path to the mypy type checker so it knows how to validate Python type hints.
explanations.139: This sets Python type checking to 'strict' mode, which catches more potential type-related bugs than the default.
explanations.140: This explicitly tells VS Code to use Python 3 from this specific path inside the Docker container.
explanations.142: This sets Pylance as the language server, which provides intelligent code completion and error detection for Python.
explanations.146: This configures the import sorting tool (isort) to use 'black' style, ensuring imports match your code formatter's expectations.
explanations.159: This defines available terminal shells and their paths inside the Linux container.
explanations.172: This disables the editor preview feature, so clicking files in the explorer opens them in a permanent tab rather than a preview.
